chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Natana (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, he said:

I saw Abdullah ibn Jundab at the station [of Arafat], and I had not seen a station more beautiful than his. He did not cease stretching his hands toward the sky while his tears flowed down his cheeks until they reached the ground. When the people departed, I said to him: O Aba Muhammad, I have never seen a station more beautiful than yours.

He said: By Allah, I only supplicated for my brothers, and that is because Aba al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) informed me that whoever supplicates for his brother in his absence, a call is made from the Throne: 'And for you is one hundred thousand fold.' So I disliked abandoning a guaranteed one hundred thousand fold for a single supplication that I do not know whether it will be accepted or not.

key_terms.العرش: The Throne of God, the highest celestial station from which divine decrees emanate
key_terms.الموقف: The station (at Arafat), the standing place during Hajj where pilgrims supplicate
key_terms.بظهر الغيب: In one's absence, behind one's back — refers to supplicating for someone who is not present
key_terms.مائة ألف ضعف: One hundred thousand fold — the multiplied reward promised for supplicating for others

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for supplicating for a fellow Muslim in their absence?
ai.summary: Ibrahim ibn Hashim recounts witnessing Abdullah ibn Jundab's deeply moving supplication at the station of Arafat, where he stood weeping with hands raised to the sky. When asked about his devotion, Abdullah explained that he only prayed for his fellow believers, because Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) had told him that whoever supplicates for a brother in his absence receives a call from God's Throne promising a hundred-thousand-fold reward. This hadith was narrated in the scholarly circles of 4th-century AH Iraq/Iran, where the audience understood the 'station' to mean the station at Arafat during the Hajj pilgrimage.
